newsitem.title: USA: Reno says she wants to stay as attorney general.
newsitem.headline: Reno says she wants to stay as attorney general.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno repeated Thursday she wants to remain in office if asked by President Clinton and said no one at the White House had ever directly criticised her performance.
"As I have said all along, if the president wanted me to stay, I would be honoured to do so," Reno told her weekly news briefing when pressed if she would stay in Clinton's second term in office.

Clinton, fresh from his re-election victory, is considering sweeping White House and other personnel changes, with at least four members of his Cabinet expected to depart. Reno was asked about news reports quoting anonymous White House sources as expressing unhappiness with her.

"As far as I'm concerned, nobody has been critical to my face or critical as a source that I can trace. I've been supported in trying to do what I think an attorney general should do, which is call the issues based on the evidence and the law and give the best legal advice possible," she said.

Reno took exception with a report the White House thinks she is not a "team player" but cannot get rid of her because of the ethical questions facing the administration. She quoted her father, a longtime reporter in Miami, as saying, "Don't believe everything you read in the newspaper."

Reno deferred to the White House when asked if she had submitted her resignation or had any meetings on her future. "That decision is up to the president and he is in the process of forming his administration for the next four years. I think any comment should be made by him," she said.

She said the Justice Department still was reviewing a request by congressional Republicans for an independent counsel to investigate allegations that Democrats engaged in illegal fund-raising activities.

Reno, who suffers from Parkinson's disease, a degenerative illness that causes trembling, said her doctors have assured her she can remain in office. Last Saturday she was among 20 Justice Department employees who worked on a local house for Habitat for Humanity, a group that builds housing for the poor. Reno said she sanded, painted and helped with cleanup.
The 58-year old Reno also described how she has gone kayaking in Maryland and has walked about halfway on an 180-mile trail from Washington, D.C., to Cumberland, Maryland.
Asked what she would do if Clinton wants her to leave, Reno replied, "I'll think about that tomorrow."
